title: A prescribed residue-field basis of a finitely presented module spreads to a basis
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ a prime ideal, and $M$ a finitely presented $A$-module (there is an exact sequence $A^{\oplus u}\to A^{\oplus v}\to M\to0$ for some $u,v\ge0$). Let $m_1,\dots,m_r\in M$ be elements whose images form a basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of the $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-vector space $M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-module-base-change], and suppose $M_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is a free $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module of rank $r$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then there is $f\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that the images $m_1/1,\dots,m_r/1$ form a basis of the localized $A_f$-module $M_f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0GWM (lemma-finitely-presented-localization-free): lift the chosen basis to a map from a finite free module and use Lemma Tag 05GF (lemma-map-between-finitely-presented) and Lemma Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local) to make that map an isomorphism after localization; this statement keeps the prescribed lifts

proof.text: (The map defined by the prescribed elements.) Let $e_1,\dots,e_r$ be the standard basis of $A^{\oplus r}$ and $\varphi:A^{\oplus r}\to M$, $(a_i)_i\mapsto\sum_ia_im_i$, so $\varphi(e_i)=m_i$; $A^{\oplus r}$ is finitely generated (by the $e_i$) [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Put $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$. Localizing at $S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], $(a_i)_i/s\mapsto(a_i/s)_i$ is an isomorphism of $A_{\mathfrak p}$-modules $(A^{\oplus r})_{\mathfrak p}\cong A_{\mathfrak p}^{\oplus r}$ (inverse $(a_i/s_i)_i\mapsto(a_i\prod_{j\ne i}s_j)_i/\prod_js_j$), so the $e_i/1$ form a basis of $(A^{\oplus r})_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]; the localized map $\varphi_{\mathfrak p}:(A^{\oplus r})_{\mathfrak p}\to M_{\mathfrak p}$, $x/s\mapsto\varphi(x)/s$, is $A_{\mathfrak p}$-linear and sends $e_i/1$ to $m_i/1$. In particular the image of $\varphi_{\mathfrak p}$ is the $A_{\mathfrak p}$-submodule generated by $m_1/1,\dots,m_r/1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0GWM (lemma-finitely-presented-localization-free): the homomorphism (y_1,...,y_n): R^n -> M

proof.text: ($\varphi_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] with $R=A$, the multiplicative subset $S$, the $A$-algebra $A_{\mathfrak p}$ (whose structure map is a localization at $S$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]), the $A$-module $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $\ell=\mathrm{id}:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ (a localization at $S$: every $s\in S$ acts bijectively on the $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, so (a)--(c) hold trivially) and the localization map $M\to M_{\mathfrak p}$. It says that $\lambda:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_AM\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $c\otimes m\mapsto c\otimes(m/1)$, is a localization at $S$. Since every $s\in S$ already acts bijectively on the $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-module $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_AM$, $\lambda$ is bijective: injective by (c) ($\lambda(x)=\lambda(y)$ gives $sx=sy$, so $x=y$) and surjective by (b) ($s^{-1}\lambda(x)=\lambda(s^{-1}x)$); it is $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-linear. By hypothesis the elements $1\otimes m_i$ (the images of the $m_i$ in $M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_AM$) span $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_AM$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, hence their images $1\otimes(m_i/1)$ span $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}$. Now $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is a finitely generated $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module (generated by the images $x_j/1$ of generators $x_j$ of $M$, which exist as $M$ is finitely presented). By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] (the form with $1\otimes x_i$ generating $\kappa\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}M_{\mathfrak p}$), $m_1/1,\dots,m_r/1$ generate $M_{\mathfrak p}$; by step 1, $\varphi_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), part (8), applied to the local ring A_p; the identification of kappa(p) (x)_A M with kappa(p) (x)_{A_p} M_p is written by the agent

proof.text: ($\varphi_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective.) By hypothesis there is an isomorphism of $A_{\mathfrak p}$-modules $\psi:M_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak p}^{\oplus r}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]; let $\theta:A_{\mathfrak p}^{\oplus r}\to(A^{\oplus r})_{\mathfrak p}$ be the isomorphism of step 1. Then $\psi\circ\varphi_{\mathfrak p}\circ\theta:A_{\mathfrak p}^{\oplus r}\to A_{\mathfrak p}^{\oplus r}$ is an $A_{\mathfrak p}$-linear endomorphism of a finitely generated $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module, surjective by step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-surjective-endomorphism-bijective] it is bijective; as $\psi$ and $\theta$ are bijective, $\varphi_{\mathfrak p}$ is injective. So $\varphi_{\mathfrak p}$ is bijective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05G8 (lemma-fun): a surjective endomorphism of a finite module is an isomorphism

proof.text: (Spreading.) $A^{\oplus r}$ is finitely generated (step 1), $M$ is finitely presented and $\varphi_{\mathfrak p}$ is bijective (steps 2, 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-to-finitely-presented-map-iso-at-prime-spreads] there is $f\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that $\varphi_f:(A^{\oplus r})_f\to M_f$, $x/f^k\mapsto\varphi(x)/f^k$, is bijective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0GWM (lemma-finitely-presented-localization-free): Lemma Tag 05GF (lemma-map-between-finitely-presented) and Lemma Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) As in step 1, $(a_i)_i/f^k\mapsto(a_i/f^k)_i$ is an isomorphism of $A_f$-modules $(A^{\oplus r})_f\cong A_f^{\oplus r}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] carrying $e_i/1$ to the $i$-th standard basis vector, and $\varphi_f(e_i/1)=m_i/1$; $\varphi_f$ is $A_f$-linear. Hence the $A_f$-linear map $A_f^{\oplus r}\to M_f$, $(c_i)_i\mapsto\sum_ic_i\,(m_i/1)$, is the composite of that isomorphism's inverse with the bijection $\varphi_f$ of step 4, so it is an isomorphism, i.e. $m_1/1,\dots,m_r/1$ form a basis of the $A_f$-module $M_f$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module].

lean.statement: theorem exists_basis_away_of_prescribed_residue_basis {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.FinitePresentation A M] (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (r : ℕ) (m : Fin r → M) (hres : ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin r) p.ResidueField (p.ResidueField ⊗[A] M), ∀ i : Fin r, b i = (1 : p.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[A] m i) (hfree : Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin r) (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl M))) : ∃ f : A, f ∉ p ∧ ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin r) (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule.Away f M), ∀ i : Fin r, b i = LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) M (m i)
